articles.excerpt: Retrouvez les photos du bord de 13ème matin !

articles.title: will the butterfly effect decide the class40 crown?
articles.excerpt:
With about 24 hours to go before the finish, the battle is raging at the front of the Class40 fleet.  Achille Nebout (Amarris) remains in the lead, but Guillaume Pirouelle (Sogestran – Seafrigo) has closed the gap by eight miles to 11.5 miles. The top 10 in the IMOCA class have now all arrived in Pointe-à-Pitre.

Marco Guerra (Imagin’Act – Socomec) has decided not to set sail again from Port-la-Forêt, bringing the total number of retirements to 19. There are now 71 skippers still racing

articles.title: how horeau won.
articles.excerpt: As is so often the case, especially in this modern era when solo skippers are basically computing their own  routes from the same weather files using the same or very similar programmes, Transatlantic races can be decided on one move which proves decisive

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 14
articles.excerpt: Ce samedi 14 novembre, 13 jours après le départ de Saint-Malo, les premiers Class40 accélèrent vers la Guadeloupe. Achille Nebout conserve les commandes, mais Guillaume Pirouelle réduit l’écart. Les arrivées se poursuivent en IMOCA, tandis que l’affaiblissement prévu de l’alizé pourrait entretenir le suspense jusqu’à Pointe-à-Pitre.

articles.title: Different strokes...
articles.excerpt: Everyone still on the Atlantic has different targets, different ambitions. Some are on course and need to consolidate, others know the clock is always ticking down. In the IMOCA class the main thing for Japan’s Masa Suzuki on Milai Furuno is qualifying for the Vendée Globe. He, like others pursuing the same dream, need to finish the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe in an elapsed time which is less than double the the winner’s time. So that means on or before the 18th November.

articles.title: Éric Péron, second in the Vintage Multi* !
articles.excerpt: As the sun rose, Éric Péron crossed the finish line of the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe this Friday, November 13, at 10:04:09 AM (local time). He completed the race aboard his ORMA trimaran, French Touch - Oceania Hotels, in 12 days, 2 hours, 2 minutes, and 9 seconds—a performance that saw him consistently among the frontrunners, often sailing neck and neck with Damien Seguin, the winner in that category.

articles.title: IMOCA : the closest finish yet!
articles.excerpt: Thursday night saw the closest and most exciting finish yet on this Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe. Thousands were glued to the tracker, refreshing it as often as possible but of course that did not tell even half of the story of sweat and tears that went on aboard the three IMOCAs At the Tête-à-l’Anglais waypoint, the order was: Sébastien Simon (Groupe Dubreuil-Air Caraïbes), Davy Beaudart (Bureau Vallée), and Maxime Sorel (Vaincre la Mucoviscidose).

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 13
articles.excerpt: Ce vendredi 13 novembre, 12 jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, la bataille reste ouverte en tête des Class40. Achille Nebout mène la course, tandis que le retour des alizés accompagne les arrivées des IMOCA en Guadeloupe. Pour une grande partie de la flotte encore en course, les vents faibles et irréguliers en bordure de l’anticyclone des Açores compliquent la tâche.

articles.title: finally, normal service is resumed
articles.excerpt: Four out of the six class winners are now known: following Tom Laperche (Ultim), Basile Bourgnon (Ocean Fifty), and Corentin Horeau (IMOCA), local hero Damien Seguin secured the title in his Rhum Multi class last night. Now only the Class40 and Rhum Mono classes have yet to be decided.

articles.title: Marco Guerra forced to retire
articles.excerpt: After a technical stopover in Port-la-Forêt, Marco Guerra, skipper of Class40 No. 207 IMAGIN'ACT–SOCOMEC, made the difficult decision not to resume his voyage to Pointe-à-Pitre. The reason: unfavorable weather conditions that made a safe crossing impossible, as did reaching Pointe-à-Pitre before the official finish line closure.

articles.title: Francesca clapcich is eighth in IMOCA
articles.excerpt: Italian-American skipper Francesca Clapcich brought her IMOCA 11th Hour Racing across the finish line of the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe at 18:41:09 hrs local time (23:41:09hrs UTC) to take eighth place from a 22 boat fleet which started the 3542 nautical miles solo Atlantic sprint from Saint Malo on Sunday 1st November.

articles.title: Damien Seguin, winner in the Vintage Multi* !
articles.excerpt: His is a triumph with a whiff of legend to it, one that Damien Seguin could reflect on when he crossed the finish line of the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe this Thursday, November 12, at 4:24:34 PM (local time).

articles.title: Sam Goodchild: fourth is not good enough, but neither is second or third
articles.excerpt:
Sam Goodchild misses IMOCA podium by 11 minutes at the end of challenging Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe

 

For Franco-Brit Sam Goodchild, skipper of MACIF Santé Prevoyance, fourth place into Gudeloupe this morning concluded what proved to be a very challenging Route du Rhum Destination Gudeloupe, suffering too many technical problems to be able to operate at close to maximum potential.

articles.title: 📸 EVERY morning, a little closer to Guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: Les jours passent et les skippers encore en mer poursuivent leur route vers la Guadeloupe ! Chaque lever et coucher de soleil offre de magnifiques couleurs sur l’Atlantique, tandis que les milles continuent de défiler. Des instants précieux capturés depuis le bord, au cœur d’une traversée qui réserve encore de belles images !

articles.title: Sam Goodchild (MACIF SANTÉ PrÉvoyance), fourth in the la Route du Rhum-Destination guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: As a favorite in this Route du Rhum—his first in the IMOCA class—Sam Goodchild faced a challenging race between Saint-Malo and Pointe-à-Pitre. Finding himself outsmarted early in the race he watched helplessly as Corentin Horeau (MACSF) pulled miles ahead, and spent the remainder of the race pushing hard to catch up with Boris Herrmann (Malizia 4). A mainsail failure and some foil issues slowed him down while passing through a tropical depression; this opening allowed Elodie Bonafous...

articles.title: Élodie Bonafous (Association Petits Princes Quéguiner) takes third place in the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe in the IMOCA class
articles.excerpt: Showing typical drive and self confidence right to the finish line, Elodie Bonafous stayed cool under pressure, holding her own against a spirited fightback from Franco-Brit Sam Goodchild (MACIF Santé Prévoyance) to take an excellent third place in the IMOCA class on the Route du Rhm Destination Guadeloupe.
